settlements.name: Hook
settlements.notes: moved to the 1:1 shoreline 2026-10-19 (was py 596: 592 m up, 6.7 km inland of the shore the open world's rule gives)

settlements.name: Ledge
settlements.notes: Moved 2026-10-23 with scale model 4.22 from 160,1007 (a water cell of the old 4.21 lake) to the north cliff over the great lake (1,638 m, ~1,340 m over the water at 298 m), where Dalab's road comes down; the arcology runs down the cliff to the shore (biomes/riftrim/PLAN.md section 12).

settlements.name: Mantis
settlements.notes: An oasis town on the Bowl's salt lake (moved 2026-10-23: from 831,816, under the 4.21 lake, to the heart of the wettest pocket on its south-west shore: Am, ~1,550 mm, -976 m, 2 km from the water; the pocket is ~330 km2 of monsoon forest and savanna in the hot desert). An Iziz holding: grew under Yuni's influence, later taken over by Izani merchant houses. Named after the Bowl mantis, a large predator of the region. See biomes/sedesert/PLAN-BOWL.md.

settlements.name: Pinnacle Rock
settlements.notes: Beast Rider roost town on a red sandstone mesa (settlements/pinnacle-rock/PLAN.md). Moved 2026-10-18 from px 737,354 (approximate) to the knoll that clears the forest: 500-600 m over the jungle floor, the K'etsaal Baatar 11 km off. Moved 2026-11-10 (the owner: 'a spot not too far that's got a bit more forest') from 1027,681, which map 5.1 left in the NE rim's savanna, 41 km west to the savage hyperjungle's north-east edge: a knoll 110 m over its 14 km round (209 m prominence), -1,287 m, Aw, 1,490 mm, 77% of the ground within 9 km jungle; the Tsékooh Baatar 17 km off (openworld/PLAN-SITES.md, openworld/pinnacle).

settlements.name: Shim
settlements.notes: restored 2026-10-18 at the seed14 position; the old Chichani capital on a lake of the Shim river (settlements/shim/PLAN.md)

settlements.name: Spirladunon
settlements.notes: The Talovolci's ceremonial settlement (the Cloud Giants). Moved 2026-10-23 from 608,798 (dry steppe in godstep valley, ~80 mm) into the cloud forest of the southern highlands: ~1.5 km, ~4,000 mm, Af, mean +18 C. LORE.md 6.21.

settlements.name: Stair
settlements.notes: The Hill arcology (kits/ancients/targets/hill), on the east flank of the springs' hollow through the Catch's interior hills, at the biggest of its five oases. A glorified campground of a couple of hundred people (merchants, caravans, arcology divers); the Ancients' tunnel from here is sealed halfway (biomes/catch/PLAN.md). Moved 2026-10-23 from 827,1113.

settlements.name: The Gate
settlements.notes: The one way into the Outlands: the Outland Gate's Narrows (1,423 m, 1.34 atm), held by the Tierhounds' long wall from wall foot to wall foot (1431,326 to 1446,326) and their toll fort and water gate on the river, with the trickster's shrine; the god's road (Sleeping City to Trickster's House) runs through it. Moved from the old 7.7 km pass (1408,414), which keeps a cairn and a shrine. biomes/outlandgate/PLAN.md section 5, biomes/outlands/PLAN.md; the owner, 2026-10-26 and 2026-11-09.

settlements.name: Trickster's House
settlements.notes: Arcoindian II (kits/ancients/targets/arcoindian2), ruined, built into the west wall of the N Outlands' main basin over the 2,132 m lake. The Coyote Men shun it as cursed: they say the trickster lives there, and the god's road ends here. biomes/outlands/PLAN.md, SURVEY.md; the owner, 2026-10-26.

settlements.name: Zey'danin
settlements.notes: Gateway to the Throne, a layered city (Zeijani, Western Islander, Izani, Hykkousoi, Voth since ~30 years ago): settlements/zeydanin/PLAN.md. Typed city 2026-10-18 (was village).

settlements.name: Ostrukh-on-Water
settlements.notes: Yuni agricultural outpost on fresh Lake Ostrukh: terrace farming, qanats, and staging for Siphon Pit expeditions.

settlements.name: Spindle Fan
settlements.notes: Yuni farming and spring outpost on the Weavers' Cradle piedmont fan: terraced crops supporting expeditions into the Loom-Chasms.

settlements.name: Tallwalls
settlements.notes: The greatest haven and fortress of the Free Giants (the Vrivolci, LORE.md 6.17, 6.21) and a sanctuary for escaped slaves of every people fleeing the Vothic Kingdom and the Realm of Dalab. Built of cyclopean columnar basalt and tier-cedar murus gallicus on the middle flood-basalt lava terrace of Greenstep (+1,980 m, Cfa/Cfb) above the confluence of the Clodosriba lava-tube rilles. Called Talodunon in their borrowed Talovolci Gaulish and Da-Talwal in Vrivolci creole. biomes/greenstep/PLAN.md.

settlements.name: Šurpu-Dhelv
settlements.notes: Zeijani cave and tuff village on the WNW flank of the Throne: fairy-chimney tuff spires and 4-level underground galleries above a braided lava tube, with covert scout tunnels toward the Zey'danin frontier (kits/zeijani/README.md, biomes/throne/NOTES.md).

settlements.name: Qarnu-Tūbu
settlements.notes: Zeijani cave and tuff village on the SSW savanna-tuff shoulder of the Throne: Moray-style terraced collapse skylights and a stepwell cistern in an ancient pahoehoe master tube, trading with the surface Ash Nomads (kits/zeijani/README.md, biomes/throne/NOTES.md).

settlements.name: Nūru-Šaplu
settlements.notes: Zeijani cave village on the ENE plume-edge shoulder of the Throne: carved into a drained parasitic magma chamber with Raufarholshellir oxidised red and purple basalt walls; center of alecap brewing and fungal alchemy (kits/zeijani/README.md, biomes/throne/NOTES.md).

settlements.name: Kolli
settlements.notes: An oasis of the Catch's crossing: the cold one: the first water down from the notch, snowmelt seeping at the north fan's toe. Izani Kold'a, Dasrī al-Kōl, Xanadui Kholṭu; caravaneers say whichever their master's tongue is. A spring and seep at a fan's toe: a pool, a reed bed, poplar and tamarisk, a well (1446 m). biomes/catch/PLAN.md sections 4 and 8; placed by scale model 5.1 edit 5 (2026-11-11).

settlements.name: Arfwai
settlements.notes: An oasis of the Catch's crossing: halfway (to Stair). Izani Afguai, Dasrī al-Ḥafwē, Xanadui Hāphwe; caravaneers say whichever their master's tongue is. A spring and seep at a fan's toe: a pool, a reed bed, poplar and tamarisk, a well (1074 m). biomes/catch/PLAN.md sections 4 and 8; placed by scale model 5.1 edit 5 (2026-11-11).

settlements.name: Bitta
settlements.notes: An oasis of the Catch's crossing: bitter water: brackish, drinkable by beasts, not by people unless boiled with ash. Izani Bit'ar, Dasrī al-Bitar, Xanadui Biṭṭar; caravaneers say whichever their master's tongue is. A spring and seep at a fan's toe: a pool, a reed bed, poplar and tamarisk, a well (1576 m). biomes/catch/PLAN.md sections 4 and 8; placed by scale model 5.1 edit 5 (2026-11-11).

settlements.name: Lasso
settlements.notes: An oasis of the Catch's crossing: the last water before the southern passes, toward Strongbow. Izani Last'a Guat'ar, Dasrī al-Lāst, Xanadui Lāsṭu; caravaneers say whichever their master's tongue is. A spring and seep at a fan's toe: a pool, a reed bed, poplar and tamarisk, a well (1509 m). biomes/catch/PLAN.md sections 4 and 8; placed by scale model 5.1 edit 5 (2026-11-11).

regions.name: Lake of Shim
regions.notes: The lake Shim stands on (its eastern shore at px 382,788): the Shim river widened, about 32 by 12 km, the river entering from the south and leaving north. To carve like the Bay of Voth (tools/scale-model/features.py, the bay pass, at the land's level here). settlements/shim/PLAN.md; the owner, 2026-10-18.

regions.name: rift rim N
regions.notes: The N rim, the glass rim (biomes/riftrim/PLAN.md section 3). Split from 'rift rim' 2026-10-23; its west end follows the w rift highland's border.

regions.name: rift rim S
regions.notes: The S rim, the black rim (biomes/riftrim/PLAN.md section 3). Split from 'rift rim' 2026-10-23, with the west bend south of the w rift highland.

regions.name: High Rift
regions.notes: Propagating eastern tip of the Great Rift between Oidong Valley and Siphon Pits: Opaline Sinter Staircase, North Mirror Graben (Lake Verdigris & Lake Cinnabar), Dorsal Wedge median horst, South Fire-and-Ice Coulee, and The Singing Gjar.

regions.name: Stalker Gate
regions.notes: Multi-branch meandering mountain and highland pass network connecting the Yuni Emirate, Stalker Range (Hub 01), Loom-Chasms, the Slabfields, and Siphon Pits around Lake Vapora.

regions.name: The Slabfields
regions.notes: The Slabfields (was Mid Basin; renamed 2026-11-12). Between the Loom-Chasms' stretching and the Siphon Pits' squeezing: north of the hinge the Loom's warp chasms die out in the basalt benches; south of it lone slabs of flood basalt stand out of the flat bench plains, thrust up and tilted as Io's mountains are (a cliff on one face, a long ramp on the other, landslide aprons below): the Anvil, the split Halves with a patera in their gap, the still-tilting Leaner over the corridor road, the Backstop. The six breached maars, the loess-and-tuff corridor and the spring-fed paterae and chasm heads are the outposts' ground; Yuni outlaws roam it. biomes/slabfields/PLAN.md; scale model 5.1 edit 7.

regions.name: neo-ozarks
regions.notes: Neo-Ozarks Dissected Carbonate & Porphyry Plateau (56,684 km²): an ancient epeirogenic tableland of flat-lying cherty dolomite and limestone (+1,260 to +1,680 m) deeply dissected by spring-fed hollows and first-magnitude karst caverns. Famous for its 5 strike-aligned exposed veins and knobs of purple-red rhyolite porphyry (+180 to +320 m ridges) where rivers carve boulder-choked canyon shut-ins.

regions.name: sasquatch tribes
regions.notes: Sasquatch Tribes High Periglacial Valleys (132,232 km²): a rugged northern rim territory east of the NW Outer Wall, cleaved by 4 steep-walled glaciated and periglacial U-troughs (Frost-Jaw Vale, Bone-Larch Hollow, Hoar-Wind Glen, and Scree-Tooth Basin at +5,850 to +6,240 m, 0.71–0.76 atm, ET/Dsc) smaller and harsher than the Yeti Kingdom's Cold Lake valley.

regions.name: spider lake
regions.notes: Spider Lake Highland Silk-Forest Basin (72,928 km²): centered on the +1,460.0 m hydrothermal highland lake (1.20 atm, 0.26 atm O₂, Cfa/Cfb). Sublacustrine warm seeps fuel year-round "lake-smoke" midge clouds that sustain permanent 200,000-strong colonies of eusocial spiders (Arachneapolita sericifera) and live rotational silk-weir arachniculture (see biomes/spiderlake/PLAN.md).

regions.name: Silent Vales
regions.notes: The Silent Vales (40,444 km²): an interconnected network of sheltered, fog-draped cool-temperate montane valleys (+1,135 to +1,890 m floors, Cfb/Csb) and two quiet ribbon lakes nestled behind the western coastal hogback ridge, draining west via a mossy water-gap gorge into the Crook River.

regions.name: tsunami coast
regions.notes: The Tsunami Coast (483,208 km²): northwestern mainland littoral zone repeatedly battered by tsunami trains generated by the explosive Steaming Seamounts. Features a wave-planed bedrock scour apron (+6 to +65 m in the SW funnel sector, +4 to +24 m in the NE Arch-shielded shadow), NW-to-SE V-shaped megatsunami boulder chevrons, backwash canyons, and perched saline plunge-pool lagoons.

regions.name: arachnoid canyons
regions.notes: Venusian Volcano-Tectonic Arachnoid Network & The Web-Cleaver Gorge: concentric ring-dike cauldrons and radial extensional fracture canyons straddling northern, eastern, and SW Korona and the southern Ria Valley rim. Cleaved by a dramatic 1,200–1,850 m-deep sinuous canyon carrying the Highland Lake river through northern Korona down into the Ria River.

regions.name: the arch
regions.notes: The Arch: an exposed undersea mid-ocean spreading ridge over the Steaming Sea (inspired by Capsica's Arch), featuring a double line of parallel rift-shoulder horst ridges (+750 to +2,150 m) with a lowered axial rift valley and drowned median sound in between, linking the northern Ria coast to the Crook.

regions.name: steaming seamounts
regions.notes: Steaming Sea Explosive Seamount Chain: a cluster of shoaling submarine volcanic calderas and Surtseyan/Krakatoan tuff cones centered in the western Arch. Periodic phreatomagmatic eruptions and flank collapses generate megatsunamis across the northwest ocean, making ports rare.

regions.name: the crook
regions.notes: The Crook: a deep tectonic trough squeezed between the western crater wall and the towering Western Boundary Cordillera. Opens at its northern neck into the Arch via a sea-level tidal fjord (0.0 m) and slopes continuously upward toward the south into a fumarolic and malachite-stained montane ecosystem.

regions.name: copper glacier
regions.notes: Copper Glacier & Crook–Rift Glacial Pass: a high-altitude alpine cryosphere in the southern Crook where glaciers grind through copper-porphyry, malachite, and azurite veins, tinting the banded ice verdigris-emerald and feeding the turquoise Copper Tarn (+2,380 m). A glaciated alpine pass extends east-southeast across the western rim to connect The Crook directly with the northwestern head of The Rift. Trimmed 2026-11-09 (scale model 5.1 edit 3) to the Firebliss Range's north edge: the range's cones and valleys are Firebliss's.

regions.name: outland gate
regions.notes: Outland Gate (NE Trans-Boundary Water-Gap Pass): a dramatic highland valley and water-gap corridor (+1,460 to +1,734 m floor framed by +4,400..+7,600 m snow peaks) breaching the northeastern rim to carry the Outland Gate River from the northern Outland lake directly into Spider Lake (see biomes/outlandgate/PLAN.md).

regions.name: ne outer wall
regions.notes: NE Outer Wall — The Glass-Skarn Bastion (101,372 km²): a structurally unique impact-crater rim bastion wedged between the Northern Korona volcano-tectonic dome, the Arachnoid radial dike swarm, Spider Lake, and the Outland Gate fault. Features 3 geothermally heated Boxwork Dike-Cauldrons (+2,670 to +2,950 m warm hydrothermal tarns), pistachio-green epidote and wine-red grossular garnet contact-metamorphic skarn badlands, and black pseudotachylite fault mirrors.

regions.name: godshearth
regions.notes: A caldera cut into the Godthrone's south flank: floor 3.6-3.75 km, walls 3-4 km high, the hot lake (3,642 m) and the spillway south. Climate (the owner, 2026-11-09): cools with height, 6 C per km from a floor of +7 C (warm month 15 C, days 24 / nights +6; cold month -2 C, days +7 / nights -10, to -18 C in the cold-air pools on clear nights): Cwb on the floor, Dwb on the benches, Dwc and ET on the rim. Rain 750-925 mm, about 70% of it in the warm half as afternoon storms, so the nights and the winters are clear (the model holds annual rain only). biomes/godshearth/PLAN.md.

regions.name: Greenstep
regions.notes: Greenstep (renamed from Green Valley): the windward, rain-drenched counterpart of Godstep Valley, descending NNW across five ponded flood-basalt lava terraces (+3,180 m to +960 m) incised by two collapsed lava-tube rilles. Captures ~1,050–1,760 mm/yr of rain (Cfa/Cfb) from prevailing NW winds and serves as the greatest refuge of the Free Giants (the Vrivolci) and escaped slaves of every people fleeing the Vothic Kingdom and the Realm of Dalab, home to their cyclopean fortress of Tallwalls (Talodunon / Da-Talwal) at px 650, 1268 (biomes/greenstep/PLAN.md).

regions.name: Labyrinth
regions.notes: The Labyrinth (250,872 km²): a Martian Noctis Labyrinthus & E/NE Chaos Terrain inversion canyon complex carved into the 4.8–6.3 km SW Glaciated Dome. Progresses from beaded pit-crater catenae in the west/south through a 3-trend intersecting polyhedral fault-graben network in the center into a collapsed Martian Chaos Terrain of isolated flat-topped horst mesas and knobby pyramids in the east/northeast opening toward The Rift and Copper Glacier.

regions.name: Firebliss Range
regions.notes: A glaciovolcanic arc on the Labyrinth's northern rim: five ice-capped stratovolcanoes (Mount Pyre 6,650 m, Cinder-Crown, Firebliss Mons, Brimstone Spire, Copper-Fissure Vent) on a 4-5 km plateau of tundra and ice, and under the spine four warm valleys with geothermal lakes (West Bliss Cauldron 2,640 m, Great Firebliss Vale 2,280 m, Solfatara Glen 2,120 m, East Bliss Vale 1,960 m; Cfb, Cfa at East Bliss), drained south-east by the Yan, Tlahn and Weyt Warra into the Labyrinth. The vents' plume blows SE over the Labyrinth. Nobody lives here; Fellgang and Kimr bands pass through semi-regularly (the owner, 2026-11-09). biomes/firebliss/PLAN.md.

regions.name: Stalker Peaks
regions.notes: East of the Catch: the ranges from its eastern wall (7-11 km) to Hub 01's high valley (~4.4-6 km; Hub 01, the ruined arcology run by a mad AI, at 1344,1409) and the 12-15 km peaks round it (1287,1293; 1321,1481; 1397,1505; 1411,1409). The Stalkers' country; no caravan takes its passes. biomes/catch/PLAN.md section 6c; scale model 5.1 edit 5 (2026-11-11).

regions.name: Hookfleet
regions.notes: Maritime corsair & harbor polity on the inner crater shore.

regions.name: Frogmen
regions.notes: Amphibious wetland territories along the western hyperjungle marshes.

regions.name: Tiguantin
regions.notes: Highland-terrace realm on the eastern crater bench.

regions.name: Jabal Shiekdom
regions.notes: Escarpment sheikhdom overlooking the southeastern Bowl.

regions.name: Kimr
regions.notes: Southwestern highland realm bordering the Labyrinth.

regions.name: crookwash
regions.notes: Alluvial and tidal outwash corridor of the central Crook, rich in established Earthly riparian flora.

regions.name: copper glacier
regions.notes: Alpine cryosphere where glaciers grind malachite and azurite copper-porphyry veins above Copper Tarn.

regions.name: crookhead
regions.notes: Upper fumarolic montane headwaters of the Crook below Copper Glacier.

regions.name: drownlands
regions.notes: Wave-swept coastal marshes and drowned fjord lowlands at the northern mouth of the Crook, dispersing Earthly coastal flora onto the SW Arch.

regions.name: the arch
regions.notes: Emergent double-ridge oceanic rift horst and axial sound bridging the Ria Delta and Steaming Seamounts.

regions.name: battered isle
regions.notes: Exposed offshore barrier island south of the Arch taking the brunt of Steaming Seamount tsunami trains.

regions.name: Scoured hills
regions.notes: Tsunami-scoured coastal headlands and chevrons south of the Ria Delta.

regions.name: ria valley
regions.notes: Great Ria River Valley: broad fertile alluvial corridor from the Dome and Spider Lake westward to the Delta; primary northern stronghold of Earth-established green flora.

regions.name: Arcflow
regions.notes: Humid windward NW piedmont and coastal river fans between the Arch neck, Ria Barrier sea-cliffs, and Ria Delta.

regions.name: heartland
regions.notes: Fertile lower-middle Ria Valley floodplain and Ancient orchard terraces where Earthly broadleaf flora is densest.

regions.name: moleshelf
regions.notes: Dissected northern piedmont bench rising from Ria Valley toward the Ria Barrier Cordillera.

regions.name: weeping valley
regions.notes: Spring-line middle Ria valley fed by karst resurgences and misty waterfalls.

regions.name: red river
regions.notes: Iron-stained upper Ria / Red River basin between Carnelian Pass, Neo-Ozarks, and the NW foot of The Dome.

regions.name: compass hills
regions.notes: Radially jointed dike-and-mesa hills along the southern Ria rim.

regions.name: Carnelian Pass
regions.notes: Sole narrow trans-cordillera pass (+2.01 km sill) threading northward from upper Ria Valley through the towering Ria Barrier Cordillera toward the Capsican Equator.

regions.name: the dome
regions.notes: The Dome Shield Volcano (~206 × 188 km): broad basaltic shield rising at gentle ~3° flank slopes from its +2.0 km polygon foot (Ria headwaters, Neo-Ozarks, Spider Lake & Tharn Hills) to a 26 km snow-rimmed summit caldera (+6,280 m rim, +5,320 m floor) with an active fumarolic nested pit crater (+4,860 m) and radial barranca gullies.

regions.name: tharn hills
regions.notes: Dry-cold windswept foothill benches east of The Dome shield volcano rising into the Tharn Uplands.

regions.name: Delta
regions.notes: Estuarine mouth of the Ria River opening onto the Arch sound; gateway for Earthly flora dispersing along the NW coast.

regions.name: Tharn Uplands
regions.notes: High cold-arid hypobaric plateau (+5.8 to +9.8 km) on the NE rim, continuous with Krator's Korona–Tharn Plume Swell.

regions.name: NW outer wall
regions.notes: Steep outer crater rim divide separating southern Ria Valley from the NW crater wall.
